properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/19/2024 to APOLLO RESOURCES LLC in Dunbar Borough, Fayette county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: APOLLO RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/19/2024
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8198916
Permit API: 051-21047
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Dunbar Borough
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/19/2024
Comments: On August 19, 2024 the Department (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection of State Game Lands 51B1 Well located in Dunbar Township, Fayette County, where violations were continued for a release from production equipment inside the green shed.At the time of this inspection, Minor rutting is developing in the access road as it enters the well site; therefore, the Department recommends the operator continue to monitor and maintain the access road as necessary in order to prevent any erosion and sedimentation events from occurring. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniformand adequate vegetative growth with the exception of the area where a production tank had previously been placed. The DEP recommends this area be seeded and mulched. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection.Two production tanks within secondary containment were observed. One of the production tanks appeared rusted but no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed. However, the tank's secondary containment was nearly full of fluid. The DEP recommends that the containment be drained, fluid be disposed of properly, and in accordance with regulations. The well tag was present at the time of this inspection. A well tag was found on the ground near wellhead. The Dept recommends the Operator permanently affix the well tag in accordance with 3211(h) . There were no observed leaks or discharge on the ground or around the wellhead. No fluid discharges were observed coming from the production tank near the wellhead onsite, however, the production tanks lid was cracked in half and open and there appeared to be a high level of fluid in this production tank. The DEP recommends the Operator replace the lid on this production tank and properly dispose of the contents within this tank to prevent a potential release. The production tank near the green shed had a hose inside the secondary containment extending out onto the ground. It appears that water in the secondary containment is being discharged to the ground as the secondary containment is at capacity. The Department recommends the removal of this excess fluid in accordance with current regulations to accommodate any potential releases that may occur. Inside the green shed located on this well site, a compressor station as well as various barrels with various unknown substances not in containment were observed. Some barrels were heavily rusted and staining in the gravel was observed underneath them as well as under the GPU and production equipment. The Department request the Operator provide information on what exactly is in the drums and what they are being used for. The Department request that this information be provided with the NOV response. The Department also recommends that the Operator remove all equipment/supplies not necessary for production.Inside the green shed, the spill that was previously observed in inspection reports 3743832 and 3808945 remains. In this green shed, the spill appears to be an oily like petroleum substance on the ground. The DEP again recommends that the Operator remediate the areas as necessary in accordance with the Department's Spill Policy. The DEP again requests the operator evaluate the releases that have occurred and provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred. The GPU unit (not in secondary containment) in this green shed had no observable active leaks or discharge.Based on today's inspection violations for the spill shall remain outstanding along with failure to have the well tag permanently affixed to the wellhead.

Comments: On May 28, 2026, the Department conducted a Compliance Schedule Evaluation of Diversified's Yasenosky 2 plugged gas well site located in Nicholson Township, Fayette County following IR 4111999, where violations were issued for failure to comply with a COA of the Department for failing to restore the plugged well site and access road. Accompanying during today's inspection is DEP ET Rosie Wise.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on March 7, 2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the site within 9 months of well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 2/17/2025, therefore the well site should be fully restored by 11/17/2025 and a well site restoration report should have been submitted to the Department by 1/16/2026. IR 4109921 documents the return of a 12/11/2025 Well Site Restoration Extension Request. At the time of this inspection, a Well Site Restoration Report with a landowner waiver of site restoration has yet to be received. At the time of this inspection, a site restoration plan was observed to be within the on-site mailbox. The access road was observed to still be graveled and unrestored with no erosion and sedimentation issues observed. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the plugged gas well site to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion and sedimentation issues observed. CFS appeared to be spread and removed from the perimeter of the plugged well site. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for failure to comply with the COA for failing to restore the plugged well site and access road is to remain outstanding at this time as the access road is still unrestored and a WSRR with a signed landowner waiver requesting the access road remain has yet to be received.

Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 6/17/2021
Comments: This admin inspection is in response to the receipt of partial analytical results for sample number 0718-177, taken on 6/7/21 as part of inspection number 3202448 on Pad B. Elevated strontium and aluminum in the analytical results indicate the release of a pollutional substance. In a call on 6/10/21 between Sean Vanfleet, DEP WQSS, and Rick Hall, representative for ARD, Mr. Hall said that there had previously been a tank containing brine on Pad B while the drilling operation was rigging up. He stated he found out from site personnel that the tank had leaked and released an estimated 20 barrels of brine onto secondary containment. Mr. Hall said that the berms on the secondary containment were not fully installed at that time and the fluid ran toward the area of the pad surface where sample 0718-177 was taken. Mr. Hall said that Creston Environmental screened the pad and found elevated conductivity in the travel lane where sample 0718-177 was taken. He said that the pad surface was scraped down to a depth of approximately 1" in this area. He said 3 boxes were filled with the excavated material. He stated that fluid with an elevated conductivity continued to seep out from beneath the secondary containment so a sump has been installed to collect this fluid. The remainder of the pad was also screened by Creston according to Rick. Creston also took a sample from the same area where sample 0718-177 was taken. Mr. Hall said that the company man did not initially report the release from the tank as he believed that the fluid had stayed on the secondary containment. Based on the estimated release volume, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation. Violations noted. Outstanding violations noted.

Comments: Site inspection at COP Tract 231 Pad A on August 28, 2020 with Rick Hall of ARD in regards to the spill reported earlier that morning. Prior to my arrival Mr. Hall was able to take some photos prior to the rain arriving. Mr. Hall's photos have been included in this inspection report. According to lease hand operator Matt Coppadge of ARD, he was manually dumping water from the dehydration unit to the produced fluids tanks via the 2" buried steel line. When Mr. Coppadge pressured back-up, he observed dust in the air and a wet spot on the surface of the well pad. He immediately stop pressurizing the line. When he assessed the well pad, he observed two holes on the surface of the well pad and a wet spot ~6-8 ft. in diameter. The release was later reported to the Department by Mr. Hall.When I arrived onsite, the well pad was wet due to the rain. Mr. Hall marked off impacted areas on the surface of the well pad based off soil screenings using a soil conductivity probe. I viewed the impacted area where the released had occurred. I screened the area using a soil probe. Soils/gravel right at the two holes on the well pad exceeded the meters range of 4.00 mS/cm. As I moved away from the holes, readings decreased. Elevated soil readings were in an area approximate 6-8 ft. in diameter. An oil sheen was observed on the well pad near the holes and in a nearby puddle of water. The contractor arrived onsite the same time I did. In addition, Matt Lock of Tuscarora Geologic & Environmental Services arrived onsite prior to my departure. Mr. Lock will be collecting samples on behalf of ARD. Please note that is 2" buried steel dump line serves all three producing Marcellus wells located on this well pad. ARD is currently unable to determine the amount of produced fluids released. Due to the unknown volume of the release, the site is required to be remediated under 78a.66 through the Act 2 process.Violations noted. - Invalid Complaint Id. - 35148

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Haralambous G 03-074 well site located in Columbia Township, Bradford County on 4/24/2023 at 1015 hours. The weather was 45 degrees with mostly cloudy skies. An Act 9 sign remains at the entrance to the well site.I met with the Repsol representative who reported to the DEP that on Friday, 4/21/2023, an unknown quantity of rainwater released off the edge of the pad surface from a tear in a secondary containment structure. Repsol reported that the rainwater impacted an area of ~12 feet by 15 feet and was field measured at ~1400us/cm. Repsol also reported that Elk Environmental was dispatched to address the incident on 4/21/2023. Elk Environmental collected samples to determine the analytics of the stormwater. During my inspection, water held within the secondary containment was field measured at ~750us/cm today. The tear in the secondary containment structure has been repaired. Pooled water off the edge of the pad surface was field measured at ~1200us/cm (photos # 2 and 3). Rainfall over the past two days has filled the secondary containment back up. Repsol reported that a water truck was scheduled to remove the additional rainwater from the containment today. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #371607 is tied to this reported incident within CTS.The four recently hydraulically fractured wells onsite remain under flowback conditions at this time. One additional preexisting well remains capable of production. Numerous temporary storage containers are held within secondary containment onsite. Pooled water on the pad surface that was field measured for electrical conductivity ranged from 220 to 750us/cm today. There was no evidence of spills/releases observed. Violations cited against API #015-23745 on 12/20/2022 and 12/28/2022 remain outstanding at this time. No additional violations are cited at this time. The DEP requests the analytical sample results from the samples collected related to the stormwater release. I departed the site at 1140 hours.

Impacted area is surrounding the wellhead and measures approximately 5’x5’. The spill appears to be localized to the wellhead area. No active leaking was observed at the time of inspection. Department contacted Operator to notify of finding and to request additional information. At 11:20 Operator (Bill Keef) returned Department’s call. Based on preliminary observations, Operator estimates less than a barrel of production fluid was released. At 15:00 Operator (Michael Bucheit) called Department to confirm Department findings and to inform that clean-up efforts have been initiated. Department informed Operator of findings and recommends Operator perform cleanup in accordance with Spill Policy. Department requests Operator follow-up with Department upon investigation of reported concerns. Department also requests Operator provide, in writing, additional information on when release occurred, cause of the release, amount and nature of material released, clean-up actions taken and anticipated clean-up timeline. Violations are being issued under 25 PA CODE 78.54 and 25 PA CODE 91.33A. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending Departmental investigation. Department will conduct follow-up inspections to monitor remediation progress. Additional violations 25 Pa. Code § 91.33(a) Failure to notify DEP of pollution incident. No phone call made forthwith.

Comments: On April 14, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The area where the water was seeping out near the northwest stormwater vault observed on March 3, 2022 was not flowing. The hole in the well pad trench liner near the northwest stormwater vault has been fixed. Two patches have been added to the trench liner. The soil in the area where the water from the seep had been pooling up has been excavated and removed. A small berm has been built in the area and a tarp has been dug in to collect stormwater. This area is being vacuumed as necessary. The DEP screened the pooled water on the downgradient side of the built berm and the conductivity was 365 uS/cm. An area to the south of the area impacted from the seep of the northwest stormwater vault that had been previously excavated to remove contaminated soil from the seep was screened for soil conductivity. The screening resulted in a measurement of 2.42 mS/cm in a small area. The area of high conductivity was shown to STL Resources Ken Shade. There was about 8 inches of water in northwest stormwater vault. About 12 inches of water was in the southwest stormwater vault. The water was not high enough in either vault to be measured for conductivity due to not being able to reach the water levels with the field water quality meter. There has been no pad surface remediation completed. The DEP screened the five seeps and three stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 20.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 21.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 26.4. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 190 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 274 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 32.6 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 40.1 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 169.4 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 23.8 uS/cm. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers. Infiltration berm 1 along the access road that had a section erode observed on February 18, 2022 has been filled in and compost filter sock has been added near the berm. The other four infiltration berms with erosion noted in Inspection Report 3324293 have been filled in. The infiltration berms along the access road have not been seeded or temporarily stabilized. It appears that earth work on the infiltration berms along the access road has been completed. The DEP recommend seeding and temporarily stabilizing the infiltration berms according to ¿102.22(b). This will help with preventing another situation of sediment discharging outside of the LOD and help prevent accelerated erosion of bare earth. Infiltration berms 1, 2, 6, 7, and 9 appear to be holding water and not infiltrating within 72 hours. The DEP recommend investigating into the functionality of these berms to avoid over topping or berm erosion. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Permit API: 015-23722
Unconventional: Yes

Municipality: Leroy Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/03/2023
Comments: Incident Inspection of Chesapeake's "SGL12 M North B" Marcellus well site.Chesapeake hydraulically fractured the 4 Marcellus wells here in November 2022.Danielle Schaad called the DEP yesterday to report an estimated 1 barrel release of production liquid to the pad surface.I spoke with Danielle Schaad and Chris Lee (both Chesapeake) on site. Lee discovered production liquid in the yellow takeout can, and moist soil around the production tank yesterday. They explained that two days ago a vac truck caused the release of production liquid while transferring it from the tank, but did not report it to Chesapeake. MR Dirt is excavating the moist pad material around the production tank. Creston Environmental and I screened the moist soil around the tank for electrical conductivity (EC) with Hanna Groline Soil Test probes. Both probes maxed out (>4.00 mS/cm). Pad material not impacted by the spill is frozen solid, and we could not get EC readings from it. Chesapeake plans to remove the production tank on Monday February 23 to excavate any impacted pad material under it. The production liquid will flow into 4 GasBuster tanks in the mean time.Violations for the spill are cited to the 015-23722 permit.Cannot assess soil stabilization today because of ~2" of snow coverage. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. I did not see any pooled water on site, just snow/ice.Air temp 8FJLP

Violation ID: 8209799
Permit API: 105-21962
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/03/2024
Comments: On 12/03/2024 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1000 hours, weather was 30F and snowing. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).The recently drilled wells onsite are currently undergoing stimulation activities (photo #2); the well permits and secondary containment inspection logs are availbe for review in the company man's trailer (photos #3 and 4).This inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by Greylock personnel on 12/03/2024 at 0115 hours. The report detailed a release of approximately 20 barrels of produced fluids onto the pad-wide secondary containment system; the released fluids accumulated at a low point of the containment system and an approximate 2 barrels of produced fluids escaped from the containment system and onto the pad surface. See CTS #: 385569 for more details.Greylock personnel met with me on site to discuss how the release happened and ongoing remediation efforts. Personnel from Penn E and R were also onsite conducting soil sampling in accordance with an Act 2 remediation plan. By the time I arrived, released fluids were already recovered and contaminated soils were being excavated and removed (photos #5 and 6). Soil screening was being conducted as material was removed to ensure that all contaminated soil is recovered. I also screened soils for electrical conductivity (EC) of the affected area; the area field measured for EC at a range of ~1.40 - >4.00mS/cm (photos #7-9).Fluids on the pad surface drain into an infiltration basin which serves as the site's post-construction stormwater management (PCSM) control (photo #10). Greylock personnel had already screened the water draining into the infiltration basin but requested that I also screen it to confirm their results. Water entering the infiltration basin field measured for EC at ~0.54mS/cm; this field measurement was consistent with Greylock's (photo #11).Hydraulic fracturing activities continue onsite (photo #12). Numerous brine, sand, temporary storage tanks/containers are noted and are held on containment (photos #13-15). The site's chemical storage area is located on containment, tidy, and all containers are labeled (photo #16). Production equipment and produced fluids tanks have been installed onsite and are to be put into use when the completed wells go into production (photo #17).Based on the results of this inspection, the following violations are cited against API #: 105-21962:- 35 P.S. 691.402(b)- 25 PA 78a.57(a)- 35 P.S. 6018.301The DEP recommends that Greylock proceeds with Act 2 remediation regarding the aforementioned release.I departed the site at 1200 hours.

Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 988343
Permit API: 129-27065
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: North Huntingdon Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/07/2023
Comments: On March 7, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection at the Bozich 2 well in North Huntingdon Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3482092 where it was found that although contaminated soil was removed from the point of impact, contamination from the stockpile was found to be leaching into the soil downslope. Recurring violations were issued as a result. The operator then explained that the tarp which was used to cover it must have been removed by inclement weather, and then proceeded to cover it with reinforced tarp and surround it with straw and silt fence. This was discussed via phone in IR 3483449. As of the date of this Admin inspection, the operator is waiting for the ground to either freeze or thaw enough for machinery to access the well site and remove the excavation stockpile. Kriebel representative Shane Kriebel roughly estimates that 20-25 gallons of fluid escaped from the tank before Kriebel acquired the well site.The following was observed:Heavy tire rutting was observed in the access road leading to the well site (see photo 1). The well site appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no concerns related to E and S or vegetative coverage (see photos 2 and 3). It was temporarily stabilized and appeared to be establishing vegetation. No staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the well head (see photo 4), and it was equipped with a well tag (see photo 5). Soil conductivity readings were taken in the formerly impacted areas around the brine tank, which appeared to be comparable to that of the surrounding soil (see photos 6-8). Additional conductivity readings were taken where contamination from the excavation stockpile was found in IR 3482092 (see photos 9-11). Elevated conductivity was found within 2 feet downslope of the stockpile. A background soil conductivity reading was taken in the crop field east of the well site, which read 230 Microsiemens (see photo 12).Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that the point of impact has been remediated and is now recovering. However, contamination from the excavation stockpile may still be impacting the soil downslope, although it does not appear to be spreading. Therefore, closure of violations shall be contingent upon submittal of waste manifest to the Department; removal and proper disposal of the excavation stockpile, and any additional impacted soil discovered underneath or downslope; and a subsequent CEI inspection. Violations remain outstanding.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/12/2023
Comments: On December 12 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the Keeno 2 OG Well in response to IR 3640044.The findings are as follows: The previosuly observed leaked appeared to be active with fluid observed emanating from the well head in the location of the plunger rod at the time of the inspection. Conductivity readings of the fluid were taken with direct reading of the water of 0.26mS and soil readings of 0.25mS and 0.04mS. Prior to leaving the location, the Department contacted Apollo Resources Representative James Stiffler to inform him of the release. I recommended that the Operator take immediate action to correct the condition creating the release and remediate the area in accordance with the Department's current spill policy. Mr. Stiffler indicated that they would send someone out to correct the leak, by either tightening any loose components or temporarily plugging the place where the leak is occurring from and remediate the area as needed. He also stated that the well is on their list to be plugged. Based on today's inspection, violations remain open for the failure to properly control production fluid and/or other fluids resulting in a release to the ground. The Department has yet to receive clarification as to what caused the release, the quantity of fluid released and how this was determined, and how long it is believed the release was occurring. Please include the clarification information within the NOV response.

Violation ID: 863843
Permit API: 117-20309
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Gaines Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-09-30
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a INCIDENT inspection at the Tilden Marcellus -Pierson 801 Well Pad located in Gaines Twp, Tioga Co. on 9/30/2019 @1300 hours in response to spill notification# 345263. The weather was 72 degrees, light rain. The spill notification report states, "Regina Logue, Regulatory/Environmental Manager for Tilden Marcellus LLC notified the phone duty officer that a spill of production water from a defective tee in a dump line occurred on 9/28/2019 at 0830 hours. The spill of 1.5 barrels occurred on the well pad. Tilden employees used a vac truck to remove liquid. Lined dumpsters and an excavator are on the way for cleanup. Tilden's well tender will be overseeing the cleanup." As of today's inspection, the area of the spill appears to be backfilled with gravel. Standing fluid on the pad surface in the area of the release had a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm. A visible flow path, from the spill location, down the fill slope through the vegetation was observed. A "Growline" soil conductivity meter was then used to test the soils in the vicinity of the flow path. The soil readings were >4.0mS/cm which is the max range of the soil meter. The elevated soil conductivity readings reached the area, at the base of the fill slope, beneath a large conifer tree. I immediately left the site to contact my Supervisor, Matt Nuss, to notify him of my findings. I then contaced Jenn Compton, Tilden Marcellus, to inquire as to why the area had been backfilled if the spill had not been remediated and Tilden Marcellus had not followed the procedure to demonstrate attainment of Act 2 standards. Ms. Compton stated she was not onsite for the cleanup over the weekend and when she checked on it this morning, she checked the wrong location onsite near the well head. She stated she had a crew and more waste containers on their way to the site to begin cleanup. I departed the area at 1430 hours. Violations of the following regulations are cited at this time against the 2H well API#117-20309: 25 Pa Code 78a.57 SWMA 301 CSL402
